title: Xor register: Floor ticket
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
A switch register toggles each indicated punch position as the ribbon advances. Mina is checking the lower stop before the ribbon press opens. A negative reading is a real measurement and must not be replaced by an invented zero.

Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading.

Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement xorRegisterFloorTicket(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Prefix bit state. Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with prefix bit state. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,4,3,3,15]. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 3.
The derived sequence is [4,0,2,6]. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 0.
The derived sequence is []. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 0.
